punchline: Brunio could not do the elastico, so he slowed it down and cut it into parts; Coyle says skill gets built in exactly those halting moments.
thirty_sec: In São Paulo, eleven-year-old Brunio kept failing at a soccer trick called the elastico. He slowed it down, split it into parts and tried again until it clicked. Daniel Coyle saw this stop-and-go rhythm in nine small training places, from a Moscow tennis court to a Dallas vocal studio. He argues that struggling at the edge of your ability builds myelin, the insulation that makes a circuit fast and clean.
